import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Carathéodory conjecture

The **Carathéodory conjecture** states that any convex, closed and twice-differentiable surface
in three-dimensional Euclidean space admits at least two umbilical points, i.e. points at which
the two principal curvatures coincide (equivalently, the second fundamental form is a scalar
multiple of the first fundamental form).

A closed convex surface is modelled as the boundary $\partial K$ of a compact convex body
$K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ with nonempty interior. The surface is $C^2$ when it is locally a
regular level set of a $C^2$ function $F$; a point $p$ of such a surface is umbilical when the
Hessian of $F$ at $p$, restricted to the tangent plane $\ker dF_p$, is a scalar multiple of the
inner product. This is the classical notion: the second fundamental form at $p$ is
$-\mathrm{Hess}\,F_p / \|\nabla F(p)\|$ on the tangent plane, for any local defining function
$F$. Flat points (both principal curvatures zero) count as umbilical.

The conjecture is known for real-analytic surfaces (Hamburger). Guilfoyle and Klingenberg
have claimed a proof for $C^{3,\alpha}$ surfaces, and Alpöge has announced a $C^\infty$
counterexample; the conjecture is currently listed as open.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: Carathéodory conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carath%C3%A9odory_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- M. Ghomi, R. Howard, *Normal curvatures of asymptotically constant graphs and Carathéodory's
  conjecture*, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 140 (2012), [arXiv:1101.3031](https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.3031)
- B. Guilfoyle, W. Klingenberg, *Proof of the Carathéodory conjecture*,
  [arXiv:0808.0851](https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.0851)
-/

open Topology
open scoped EuclideanGeometry InnerProductSpace

namespace CaratheodoryConjecture

/-- `F` is a *local $C^2$ defining function* for the set `S ⊆ ℝ³` at the point `p`: `F` is twice
continuously differentiable near `p`, its derivative at `p` is nonzero (so its zero set is a
regular surface near `p`), and `S` coincides with the zero set of `F` in a neighbourhood of `p`. -/
structure IsLocalDefiningFunction (S : Set ℝ³) (p : ℝ³) (F : ℝ³ → ℝ) : Prop where
  contDiffAt : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 F p
  fderiv_ne_zero : fderiv ℝ F p ≠ 0
  eventually_mem_iff : ∀ᶠ x in 𝓝 p, x ∈ S ↔ F x = 0

/-- A set `S ⊆ ℝ³` is a *$C^2$ surface* (an embedded, twice continuously differentiable surface)
if near each of its points it is a regular level set of a $C^2$ function. -/
def IsC2Surface (S : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∀ p ∈ S, ∃ F : ℝ³ → ℝ, IsLocalDefiningFunction S p F

/-- A point `p` of a set `S ⊆ ℝ³` is an *umbilical point* of `S` if `S` has a local $C^2$ defining
function `F` at `p` whose Hessian at `p`, restricted to the tangent plane $\ker dF_p$, is a scalar
multiple `κ` of the inner product. Since the second fundamental form of a $C^2$ surface at `p` is
$-\mathrm{Hess}\,F_p / \|\nabla F(p)\|$ on the tangent plane, this says exactly that the two
principal curvatures of `S` at `p` coincide (including the case where both vanish). -/
def IsUmbilicalPoint (S : Set ℝ³) (p : ℝ³) : Prop :=
  p ∈ S ∧ ∃ F : ℝ³ → ℝ, IsLocalDefiningFunction S p F ∧ ∃ κ : ℝ,
    ∀ v w : ℝ³, fderiv ℝ F p v = 0 → fderiv ℝ F p w = 0 →
      fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ F) p v w = κ * ⟪v, w⟫_ℝ

/-- The function $x \mapsto \|x\|^2 - 1$ is a local defining function for the unit sphere at each
of its points. -/
@[category test, AMS 53]
theorem isLocalDefiningFunction_sphere (p : ℝ³) (hp : p ∈ Metric.sphere (0 : ℝ³) 1) :
    IsLocalDefiningFunction (Metric.sphere (0 : ℝ³) 1) p (fun x ↦ ‖x‖ ^ 2 - 1) where
  contDiffAt := ((contDiff_id.norm_sq ℝ).sub contDiff_const).contDiffAt
  fderiv_ne_zero := by
    have h : fderiv ℝ (fun x : ℝ³ ↦ ‖x‖ ^ 2 - 1) p = 2 • innerSL ℝ p :=
      ((hasStrictFDerivAt_norm_sq p).hasFDerivAt.sub_const 1).fderiv
    rw [h]
    intro h0
    have := congrArg (fun L : ℝ³ →L[ℝ] ℝ ↦ L p) h0
    simp [mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm.mp hp] at this
  eventually_mem_iff := Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun x ↦ by
    simp [sub_eq_zero, pow_eq_one_iff_of_nonneg (norm_nonneg x) two_ne_zero]

/-- The unit sphere is a $C^2$ surface. -/
@[category test, AMS 53]
theorem isC2Surface_sphere : IsC2Surface (Metric.sphere (0 : ℝ³) 1) :=
  fun p hp ↦ ⟨_, isLocalDefiningFunction_sphere p hp⟩

/-- Every point of the unit sphere is umbilical. -/
@[category test, AMS 53]
theorem isUmbilicalPoint_sphere (p : ℝ³) (hp : p ∈ Metric.sphere (0 : ℝ³) 1) :
    IsUmbilicalPoint (Metric.sphere (0 : ℝ³) 1) p := by
  refine ⟨hp, _, isLocalDefiningFunction_sphere p hp, 2, fun v w _ _ ↦ ?_⟩
  have h : fderiv ℝ (fun x : ℝ³ ↦ ‖x‖ ^ 2 - 1) = fun x ↦ (2 • innerSL ℝ) x := by
    ext x : 1
    exact ((hasStrictFDerivAt_norm_sq x).hasFDerivAt.sub_const 1).fderiv
  rw [h, ContinuousLinearMap.fderiv]
  simp

/--
**Carathéodory conjecture.** Any convex, closed and twice-differentiable surface in
three-dimensional Euclidean space admits at least two umbilical points.

Precisely: let $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ be a compact convex set with nonempty interior whose
boundary $\partial K$ is a $C^2$ surface. Then $\partial K$ has at least two distinct umbilical
points, i.e. points at which the two principal curvatures coincide.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52 53]
theorem caratheodory_conjecture (K : Set ℝ³) (hK : Convex ℝ K) (hKc : IsCompact K)
    (hKi : (interior K).Nonempty) (hS : IsC2Surface (frontier K)) :
    ∃ p q, p ≠ q ∧ IsUmbilicalPoint (frontier K) p ∧ IsUmbilicalPoint (frontier K) q := by
  sorry

end CaratheodoryConjecture

modeling_decisions: 'Convex, closed surface' is modelled as the boundary `frontier K` of a compact convex set K ⊆ ℝ³ with nonempty interior (as prescribed by the decomposition table). The nonempty-interior hypothesis is essential: for K = ∅ the frontier is empty, `IsC2Surface ∅` holds vacuously and the conclusion would be false; degenerate lower-dimensional convex sets are also excluded. Strict convexity is NOT assumed (only 'convex' in the statement), so flat pieces are allowed.

'Twice-differentiable' is formalised as C² (ContDiffAt ℝ 2 F p for a local defining function), following the decomposition table and Ghomi–Howard's C² formulation, rather than mere twice-differentiability without continuity of the second derivative.

The surface regularity is expressed via local regular level sets (IsLocalDefiningFunction) rather than local graphs after a rigid motion or a C² embedding of S²; these are all equivalent for embedded C² surfaces (implicit function theorem), and the level-set form avoids coordinate bookkeeping. ContDiffAt (C² on some neighbourhood of p) is used rather than global ContDiff; the two are equivalent by cutting off with a bump function.

Umbilic is defined as: the Hessian fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ F) p of a local defining function F, restricted to the tangent plane ker (fderiv ℝ F p), equals κ·⟪·,·⟫ for some real κ. For a C² surface this is independent of the choice of F (if G is another defining function then dG_p = c·dF_p and Hess G|_T = c·Hess F|_T), and equals the classical condition κ₁ = κ₂ because II = −Hess F|_T/‖∇F‖. The definition uses ∃ F (a witness) rather than ∀ F, which avoids vacuous truth at non-C² points; both readings coincide on C² surfaces. The sign convention is irrelevant since κ is existentially quantified. Flat points (κ = 0) count as umbilical, consistent with the table.
'At least two umbilical points' is formalised as ∃ p q, p ≠ q ∧ IsUmbilicalPoint (frontier K) p ∧ IsUmbilicalPoint (frontier K) q — distinct points, no index/multiplicity counting.

Category kept as `research open` per the task despite the Wikipedia article's mention of an announced C^∞ counterexample (Alpöge) and a claimed C^{3,α} proof (Guilfoyle–Klingenberg); the module docstring records these as claims/announcements only.

Three `category test` theorems (with proofs) check the definitions on the unit sphere: ‖x‖²−1 is a local defining function, the sphere is a C² surface, and every point of the sphere is umbilical (κ = 2). These show the hypotheses of the conjecture are satisfiable and the umbilic notion is not vacuous.

/-!
# Carathéodory conjecture

The Carathéodory conjecture asserts that a closed convex $C^2$ surface in Euclidean
three-space has at least two umbilic points.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Carathéodory conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carath%C3%A9odory_conjecture)
-/

namespace CaratheodoryConjecture

local notation "E2" => EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)
local notation "E3" => EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)

/--
`IsLocalC2Parametrization S p φ q` says that `φ` regularly and injectively parametrizes an
open piece of `S` around `p`, with `φ q = p`, and is twice continuously differentiable there.
-/
def IsLocalC2Parametrization (S : Set E3) (p : E3) (φ : E2 → E3) (q : E2) : Prop :=
  ∃ U : Set E2, ∃ V : Set E3,
    IsOpen U ∧ q ∈ U ∧ IsOpen V ∧ p ∈ V ∧
      ContDiffOn ℝ 2 φ U ∧ Set.InjOn φ U ∧
      Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ φ q) ∧ φ q = p ∧ φ '' U = S ∩ V

/-- A subset of Euclidean three-space which is locally a $C^2$ embedded surface. -/
def IsC2EmbeddedSurface (S : Set E3) : Prop :=
  ∀ p ∈ S, ∃ (φ : E2 → E3) (q : E2), IsLocalC2Parametrization S p φ q

/--
A point is umbilic when, in a local regular parametrization, the second fundamental form is a
scalar multiple of the first fundamental form. The normal is not normalized, so its scaling is
absorbed by the scalar. This definition includes flat points.
-/
def IsUmbilicPoint (S : Set E3) (p : E3) : Prop :=
  ∃ (φ : E2 → E3) (q : E2), IsLocalC2Parametrization S p φ q ∧
    ∃ n : E3, n ≠ 0 ∧
      (∀ u : E2, inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ φ q u) n = 0) ∧
      ∃ κ : ℝ, ∀ u v : E2,
        inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ φ) q u v) n =
          κ * inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ φ q u) (fderiv ℝ φ q v)

/--
The **Carathéodory conjecture**: the $C^2$ boundary of every compact convex subset of
three-dimensional Euclidean space with nonempty interior has at least two distinct umbilic
points.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 53]
theorem caratheodory_conjecture :
    ∀ K : Set E3, Convex ℝ K → IsCompact K → (interior K).Nonempty →
      IsC2EmbeddedSurface (frontier K) →
        ∃ p ∈ frontier K, ∃ q ∈ frontier K,
          p ≠ q ∧ IsUmbilicPoint (frontier K) p ∧ IsUmbilicPoint (frontier K) q := by
  sorry

end CaratheodoryConjecture
modeling_decisions: Following the decomposition and the background article's C² formulation, a closed convex surface is represented as the frontier of a compact convex subset of Euclidean ℝ³ with nonempty interior; compactness supplies closedness.

A C² embedded surface is expressed by injective local regular parametrizations from Euclidean ℝ² whose images are the intersection of the surface with an ambient open neighborhood. `ContDiffOn ℝ 2` formalizes twice continuous differentiability.

An umbilic point is defined in a local regular parametrization by requiring the normal component of the second derivative (the second fundamental form, up to normalization of the normal) to be a scalar multiple of the pullback Euclidean inner product (the first fundamental form). The normal is required to be nonzero and orthogonal to all tangent vectors.
The umbilic definition is existential in the choice of local parametrization. The defining proportionality is invariant under regular changes of coordinates and normal rescaling.
Flat points are included: the scalar in the proportionality condition may be zero.
At least two points is represented by two surface points with an explicit inequality, ensuring distinctness without relying on the default behavior of `Set.ncard` for infinite sets.
The declaration remains tagged `research open` as required, notwithstanding the background article's mention of an announced future C∞ counterexample.

claimed a proof for $C^{3,\alpha}$ surfaces, and a $C^\infty$ counterexample has been announced,

- [Wikipedia, Carathéodory conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carath%C3%A9odory_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- M. Ghomi, R. Howard, *Normal curvatures of asymptotically constant graphs and Carathéodory's
  conjecture*, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 140 (2012), [arXiv:1101.3031](https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.3031)
- B. Guilfoyle, W. Klingenberg, *Proof of the Carathéodory conjecture*,
  [arXiv:0808.0851](https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.0851)

open Topology
open scoped EuclideanGeometry InnerProductSpace

namespace CaratheodoryConjecture

/-- `φ` is a regular `C²` local parametrisation of the set `S ⊆ ℝ³` around the point `p`, defined
on the open set `U ⊆ ℝ²`: it is `C²` on `U`, its derivative is injective at every point of `U`,
and it is a homeomorphism from `U` onto `S ∩ W` for some open neighbourhood `W` of `p` in `ℝ³`.
Sets admitting such a parametrisation around each of their points are exactly the regular
`C²` surfaces (do Carmo, *Differential Geometry of Curves and Surfaces*, §2-2). -/
structure IsLocalParam (S : Set ℝ³) (p : ℝ³) (U : Set ℝ²) (φ : ℝ² → ℝ³) : Prop where
  isOpen : IsOpen U
  contDiffOn : ContDiffOn ℝ 2 φ U
  fderiv_injective : ∀ u ∈ U, Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ φ u)
  isEmbedding : IsEmbedding (U.restrict φ)
  exists_image_eq : ∃ W : Set ℝ³, IsOpen W ∧ p ∈ W ∧ φ '' U = S ∩ W

/-- A set `S ⊆ ℝ³` is a regular `C²` surface if it admits a regular `C²` local parametrisation
around each of its points. -/
def IsC2Surface (S : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∀ p ∈ S, ∃ U φ, IsLocalParam S p U φ

/-- A point `p` of a set `S ⊆ ℝ³` is an umbilical point of `S` if, for a regular `C²` local
parametrisation `φ` of `S` around `p` with `φ u = p`, the second fundamental form at `u`,
$(v, w) \mapsto \langle D^2\varphi(u)(v, w), n\rangle$ where `n` is a unit normal vector, is a
scalar multiple of the first fundamental form
$(v, w) \mapsto \langle D\varphi(u)v, D\varphi(u)w\rangle$.
Equivalently, the two principal curvatures of `S` at `p` coincide. The condition does not depend
on the choice of the parametrisation or of the sign of the unit normal. Flat points, where both
principal curvatures vanish, are umbilical points. -/
def IsUmbilicalPoint (S : Set ℝ³) (p : ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ (U : Set ℝ²) (φ : ℝ² → ℝ³) (u : ℝ²), IsLocalParam S p U φ ∧ u ∈ U ∧ φ u = p ∧
    ∃ n : ℝ³, ‖n‖ = 1 ∧ (∀ v, ⟪fderiv ℝ φ u v, n⟫_ℝ = 0) ∧
      ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ v w, ⟪fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ φ) u v w, n⟫_ℝ = c * ⟪fderiv ℝ φ u v, fderiv ℝ φ u w⟫_ℝ

/-- An umbilical point of `S` lies on `S`. -/
@[category API, AMS 53]
theorem IsUmbilicalPoint.mem {S : Set ℝ³} {p : ℝ³} (h : IsUmbilicalPoint S p) : p ∈ S := by
  obtain ⟨U, φ, u, hφ, hu, rfl, -⟩ := h
  obtain ⟨W, -, -, hW⟩ := hφ.exists_image_eq
  exact (hW ▸ Set.mem_image_of_mem φ hu).1

/-- **Carathéodory conjecture.** Any convex, closed and twice-differentiable surface in
three-dimensional Euclidean space admits at least two umbilical points.

The surface is the boundary $\partial K$ of a convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ (a compact
convex set) with nonempty interior, and $\partial K$ is assumed to be a regular $C^2$ surface.
The conclusion is that $\partial K$ has at least two distinct umbilical points, counted without
multiplicity or index. -/
@[category research open, AMS 52 53]
theorem caratheodory_conjecture (K : ConvexBody ℝ³) (hK : (interior (K : Set ℝ³)).Nonempty)
    (hS : IsC2Surface (frontier (K : Set ℝ³))) :
    2 ≤ {p | IsUmbilicalPoint (frontier (K : Set ℝ³)) p}.encard := by
  sorry

end CaratheodoryConjecture

modeling_decisions: 'Convex, closed surface' is modelled as the boundary `frontier K` of a compact convex set `K : ConvexBody ℝ³` with nonempty interior (so the boundary is a genuine closed surface, homeomorphic to S²). def IsLocalDefiningFunction (S : Set E) (p : E) (f : E → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f p ∧ fderiv ℝ f p ≠ 0 ∧ S =ᶠ[𝓝 p] {x | f x = 0}

/-!
# Carathéodory conjecture

The Carathéodory conjecture states that any convex, closed and twice-differentiable surface in
three-dimensional Euclidean space admits at least two umbilical points, i.e. points at which the
two principal curvatures coincide.

Following Ghomi–Howard, a *closed convex surface* is the boundary of a compact convex set with
nonempty interior in $\mathbb{R}^3$, and the surface is required to be of class $C^2$, the
minimal regularity for which umbilical points are well defined. A point $p$ of a $C^2$ surface
$S$ is *umbilical* if the second fundamental form of $S$ at $p$ is a scalar multiple of the first
fundamental form; flat points (both principal curvatures zero) are included.

Mathlib has no notion of the second fundamental form, so we describe $C^2$ surfaces by local
defining functions: near each of its points, $S$ is the regular zero set of a $C^2$ function
$F$. The tangent plane at $p$ is then $\ker dF_p$, and the second fundamental form of $S$ at $p$
(with respect to the unit normal $\nabla F_p / \|\nabla F_p\|$) is $-D^2F_p / \|\nabla F_p\|$
restricted to the tangent plane. Hence $p$ is umbilical iff $D^2F_p(v, w) = c \langle v, w\rangle$
for all tangent vectors $v, w$ and some constant $c$; this does not depend on the choice of $F$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Carathéodory conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carath%C3%A9odory_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- M. Ghomi, R. Howard, *Normal curvatures of asymptotically constant graphs and Carathéodory's
  conjecture*, [arXiv:1101.3031](https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.3031)
- B. Guilfoyle, W. Klingenberg, *Proof of the Carathéodory conjecture*,
  [arXiv:0808.0851](https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.0851)
-/

open scoped EuclideanGeometry InnerProductSpace

namespace CaratheodoryConjecture

/-- `F` is a *local `C²` defining function* of the set `S ⊆ ℝ³` at `p` on `V`: the set `V` is an
open neighbourhood of `p`, `F` is `C²` on `V` with nowhere vanishing derivative on `V`, and the
points of `S` in `V` are exactly the zeros of `F` in `V`. -/
structure IsLocalDefiningFun (S : Set ℝ³) (p : ℝ³) (F : ℝ³ → ℝ) (V : Set ℝ³) : Prop where
  isOpen : IsOpen V
  mem : p ∈ V
  contDiffOn : ContDiffOn ℝ 2 F V
  fderiv_ne_zero : ∀ x ∈ V, fderiv ℝ F x ≠ 0
  mem_iff : ∀ x ∈ V, x ∈ S ↔ F x = 0

/-- A set `S ⊆ ℝ³` is a *`C²` surface* if near each of its points it is the regular zero set of
a `C²` function, i.e. `S` is a `C²` embedded submanifold of `ℝ³` of dimension two. -/
def IsC2Surface (S : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∀ p ∈ S, ∃ F V, IsLocalDefiningFun S p F V

/-- A point `p` of a set `S ⊆ ℝ³` is an *umbilical point* of `S` if `S` is a `C²` surface near
`p` and the second fundamental form of `S` at `p` is a scalar multiple of the first fundamental
form, i.e. the two principal curvatures of `S` at `p` coincide. In terms of a local defining
function `F` of `S` at `p`, this says that `D²F_p (v, w) = c * ⟪v, w⟫` for some constant `c` and
all `v, w` in the tangent plane `ker dF_p`. Flat points (`c = 0`) are umbilical. -/
def IsUmbilicalPoint (S : Set ℝ³) (p : ℝ³) : Prop :=
  p ∈ S ∧ ∃ F V, IsLocalDefiningFun S p F V ∧ ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ v w : ℝ³,
    fderiv ℝ F p v = 0 → fderiv ℝ F p w = 0 → iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 F p ![v, w] = c * ⟪v, w⟫_ℝ

/-- **Carathéodory conjecture.** Any convex, closed and twice-differentiable surface in
three-dimensional Euclidean space admits at least two umbilical points.

Precisely: if $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ is a compact convex set with nonempty interior whose
boundary $\partial K$ is a $C^2$ surface, then $\partial K$ has at least two distinct umbilical
points, i.e. points at which the two principal curvatures of $\partial K$ coincide. -/
@[category research open, AMS 52 53]
theorem caratheodory_conjecture (K : ConvexBody ℝ³) (hK : (interior (K : Set ℝ³)).Nonempty)
    (hS : IsC2Surface (frontier (K : Set ℝ³))) :
    ∃ p q, p ≠ q ∧ IsUmbilicalPoint (frontier (K : Set ℝ³)) p ∧
      IsUmbilicalPoint (frontier (K : Set ℝ³)) q := by
  sorry

/-- The function `x ↦ ‖x‖² - 1` is a local `C²` defining function of the unit sphere at each of
its points. -/
@[category test, AMS 52 53]
theorem isLocalDefiningFun_sphere (p : ℝ³) (hp : p ∈ Metric.sphere (0 : ℝ³) 1) :
    IsLocalDefiningFun (Metric.sphere (0 : ℝ³) 1) p (fun x => ‖x‖ ^ 2 - 1) {0}ᶜ where
  isOpen := isOpen_compl_singleton
  mem := by
    simp only [Set.mem_compl_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
    rintro rfl
    simp at hp
  contDiffOn := ((contDiff_norm_sq ℝ).sub contDiff_const).contDiffOn
  fderiv_ne_zero x hx h := by
    rw [((hasStrictFDerivAt_norm_sq x).hasFDerivAt.sub_const 1).fderiv] at h
    have := congrArg (fun f => f x) h
    simp at this
    exact hx this
  mem_iff x _ := by
    rw [mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm, sub_eq_zero, pow_eq_one_iff_of_nonneg (norm_nonneg x) two_ne_zero]

/-- The unit sphere is a `C²` surface. -/
@[category test, AMS 52 53]
theorem isC2Surface_sphere : IsC2Surface (Metric.sphere (0 : ℝ³) 1) :=
  fun p hp => ⟨_, _, isLocalDefiningFun_sphere p hp⟩

/-- Every point of the unit sphere is umbilical. -/
@[category test, AMS 52 53]
theorem isUmbilicalPoint_sphere (p : ℝ³) (hp : p ∈ Metric.sphere (0 : ℝ³) 1) :
    IsUmbilicalPoint (Metric.sphere (0 : ℝ³) 1) p := by
  refine ⟨hp, _, _, isLocalDefiningFun_sphere p hp, 2, fun v w _ _ => ?_⟩
  have h1 : fderiv ℝ (fun x : ℝ³ => ‖x‖ ^ 2 - 1) = fun x => 2 • innerSL ℝ x := by
    ext x : 1
    exact ((hasStrictFDerivAt_norm_sq x).hasFDerivAt.sub_const 1).fderiv
  have h2 : (fun x : ℝ³ => 2 • innerSL ℝ x) = ⇑(2 • innerSL ℝ) := by
    ext x : 1
    simp
  rw [iteratedFDeriv_two_apply, h1, h2, ContinuousLinearMap.fderiv]
  simp

end CaratheodoryConjecture
